scalars.scalar_value: Education: Possession of a bachelor’s degree in business, public, or non-profit administration, accounting, finance, or related field.

Experience: Four years of experience performing professional accounting or payroll duties, preferably in a public K-12 education setting. Two years of experience as a supervisor of accounting or payroll staff are also required (in addition to, or as part of, the professional accounting or payroll experience).

items.item_text: 01. Describe your experience in performing professional accounting operations, accounts payable, payroll administration, fiscal services, or related business functions, preferably in a public K-12 education setting. Ensure the experience described is also reflected in the work experience section of your application. (300 words max)

02. Describe your supervisory or leadership experience in a finance or payroll environment. Include the scope of your responsibilities and the types of staff or functions you led. Ensure the experience described is also reflected in the work experience section of your application. (300 words max)

03. Describe your experience in preparing financial records and in reviewing, advising, and providing policy direction and input on complex business concepts, statutes, policies and strategies. (300 words max)

04. I understand that SBCEO has an in-person work culture, and this position is designated as fully in-person at the site listed on the position announcement and may require travel throughout the county. I also understand that any request for a remote work arrangement will be reviewed in accordance with applicable laws and SBCEO’s remote work policy and procedure. Remote work arrangements are granted at SBCEO’s sole discretion. Options: Yes | No

05. The hiring range for this job is $133,827 - $163,056. If you were offered the position, would you be able to accept it at a salary in that range? If yes, please specify what salary in that range you would be willing to accept.
Education: Possession of a bachelor’s degree in business, public, or non-profit administration, accounting, finance, or related field.

Experience: Four years of experience performing professional accounting or payroll duties, preferably in a public K-12 education setting. Two years of experience as a supervisor of accounting or payroll staff are also required (in addition to, or as part of, the professional accounting or payroll experience).
Equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience that provide the required knowledge and abilities will also be considered.
A typical way to qualify for this classification would be:
Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Generally Accepted Audit Standards (GAAS), and Governmental Accounting Standards (GAS)
Learn the operations, policies, practices, and objectives of the County Education Office
Principles, practices, and procedures of governmental accounting, payroll administration, budgeting, auditing, and financial reporting
Plan, organize, and prioritize work of self and others
Applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, codes, and reporting requirements related to payroll and fiscal services
Interpret, apply, and explain laws, regulations, policies, contracts, and technical procedures
Payroll systems, financial software applications, database systems, and automated reporting tools
Analyze situations and data accurately, exercise sound judgment, and adopt an effective course of action
Public agency defined benefit retirement systems
Identify problems, evaluate alternatives, and implement effective solutions
Internal control practices and audit procedures
Coordinate and execute multiple projects, timelines, and reporting requirements
Principles of budget development and management
Draft a variety of written materials, including policies, procedures, correspondence, and reports
Principles and practices of competitive bidding and public contracting
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those supervised, individuals at all levels of districts served, and other stakeholders
Data collection and management methods
Work independently and as member or leader of a team
Strategic planning
Lead and work effectively with groups to accomplish goals and consistently meet timelines
Principles of supervision, training and professional development, and performance evaluation
Train and provide technical guidance to staff and stakeholders
Correct English usage, grammar, spelling, punctuation and vocabulary
Make accurate arithmetical computations
Arithmetic, including percentages and fractions
Use a variety of computerized accounting, enterprise, and other software programs
Modern office practices, procedures, and technology
Understand and follow oral and written directions
Standard office productivity software applications
Meet schedules and deadlines
Telephone and email etiquette
Maintain confidentiality of sensitive financial and personnel information
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing
